selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is whether a multimodal multiprofile setup with a strong pretrained image encoder provides a promising baseline. This config tests that core direction using stable choices (PCA RNA, ViT-L image, average pooling, concatenation), giving an informative anchor for later comparisons of RNA encoders, aggregation, and fusion while avoiding overcommitting to complex components too early.

The only completed experiment, config_002, gives a sparse but useful baseline: multimodal multiprofile with PCA RNA, ViT-L image, avgpool, and concat fusion achieves 0.629 accuracy and 0.599 F1. The most important nearby uncertainty is whether weighted fusion can improve on simple concatenation while keeping the same promising encoders and aggregation. config_009 changes only fusion from concat to weighted, so it cleanly tests this design choice. Under the limited budget, this minimal perturbation is a strong exploitation/exploration balance: it can either identify a better fusion rule or confirm that concat is already near-optimal for this backbone.

The only completed evidence shows that, with the same multimodal multiprofile setup using pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion outperforms concat fusion in both accuracy and F1. The key uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool while retaining the better weighted fusion. config_005 makes this minimal, controlled change, so it exploits the current best direction while testing an important architectural choice with 7 experiments remaining.

The strongest evidence so far is config_009: multimodal multiprofile with pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, and weighted fusion, achieving 0.6352 accuracy and 0.6183 F1, while transformer aggregation was clearly worse. config_016 keeps this promising architecture fixed and only changes the RNA encoder to scgpt, directly testing whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA in the currently best region. With 6 experiments remaining, this is a high-value exploitation/exploration step because it probes the largest untested design axis without abandoning the strongest known configuration.

The current best evidence favors PCA_n2000, avgpool, and weighted fusion: config_009 (PCA, ViT, avgpool, weighted) is best at 0.635 accuracy / 0.618 F1, outperforming concat fusion, transformer aggregation, and scgpt. The main untested factor in this promising setting is the image encoder. config_029 changes only the image encoder to resnet50 while keeping PCA_n2000, avgpool, and weighted fusion, so it tests whether a lighter image encoder can match or beat ViT. With 5 experiments remaining, this is a low-risk, high-information single-factor extension of the current best configuration.

The strongest evidence is for multimodal multiprofile with avgpool and weighted fusion, with PCA2000 + resnet50 currently best (0.639) and transformer aggregation or scgpt + ViT performing poorly. The main remaining uncertainty is the RNA encoder, since scvi_n200 is untested. This experiment tests scvi_n200 while keeping the best known image encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed, clarifying whether a learned RNA encoder can improve on PCA without confounding other choices.

The strongest result is config_049 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted, acc 0.6776, F1 0.6464), and avgpool/weighted have generally outperformed alternatives in the tested space. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the scvi_n200 RNA encoder benefits from the stronger imagenet_vit_l image encoder. config_045 tests this as a single-factor extension of the current best by changing only the image encoder, making it a high-value exploitation step while still leaving budget to follow up on the better image encoder or aggregation choice.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted multiprofile is the current best (0.706 accuracy), and weighted fusion has generally outperformed concat in tested comparisons. The main remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for this best encoder pair, since transformer was previously tested mainly with pca_n2000 and performed poorly. config_024 keeps the proven scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, and weighted fusion settings while testing transformer aggregation, making it the best exploitation step with 2 experiments left: if it improves, it may become the new best; if not, it confirms avgpool as the preferred aggregation for the leading configuration.

The strongest evidence is scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, which is the current best at 0.725 accuracy, and transformer aggregation clearly improved over avgpool in this setting. The main remaining uncertainty is whether concat fusion could match or beat weighted fusion when combined with the best RNA/image/aggregation choices. config_018 tests this direct extension of the current best configuration; it has a reasonable chance of being competitive, and its result will clarify whether the final experiment should prioritize weighted or concat fusion variants.

The strongest evidence favors scvi_n200 RNA encoding, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion: config_024 is the current best at 0.725, config_018 is close with concat, and config_045 shows scvi_n200 + ViT is already strong. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer/weighted benefit generalizes to resnet50, since scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted already reached 0.678. config_007 tests that logical extension while retaining the best-performing RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion, making it the most promising untested choice for the final experiment.
